questions.question: Under the Sukanya Samriddhi Account Yojana, minimum how much money needs to be deposited in one financial year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs. 250**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under the Sukanya Samriddhi Account Yojana, the minimum amount that needs to be deposited in one financial year is **Rs. 250**.
 
• The scheme encourages parents or guardians to save for the education and marriage expenses of their girl child.
 
• Deposits can be made in multiples of Rs. 50, with a maximum limit of Rs. 1.5 lakh per financial year.
 
• The account can be opened anytime from the birth of the girl child till she attains the age of 10 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The account offers an attractive interest rate which is revised quarterly by the government.
 
• It provides tax benefits under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, and the interest earned and maturity amount are exempted from tax.
 
• The account reaches maturity after 21 years from the date of opening or upon the marriage of the girl child after she turns 18, whichever is earlier.
 
• Partial withdrawals up to 50% of the account balance are allowed once the girl child reaches the age of 18 for her higher education or marriage expenses.

questions.question: Which phenomenon is opposite to solidification?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fusion**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fusion** is the process that is opposite to solidification.
 
• In **solidification**, a liquid turns into a solid. Conversely, in **fusion**, a solid turns into a liquid.
 
• Fusion is also commonly known as **melting**.
 
• This phenomenon occurs when a substance absorbs heat, causing its molecules to vibrate faster and eventually overcome the forces holding them in a solid structure.
 
• Examples of fusion include ice melting into water and wax melting when heated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sublimation** is a process where a solid changes directly into a gas without passing through the liquid phase.
 
• **Vaporisation** refers to the process of a liquid turning into a gas, either through evaporation or boiling.
 
• **Condensation** is the process where a gas turns into a liquid.
 
• Understanding these processes is crucial in fields such as chemistry, physics, and engineering.
 
• Each of these processes involves energy changes and plays a significant role in various natural and industrial applications.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that, where the same person is appointed as the Governor of two or more states, the emoluments and allowances payable to him/her shall be allocated among those states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 158**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 158** of the Indian Constitution mentions that, where the same person is appointed as the Governor of two or more states, the emoluments and allowances payable to him/her shall be allocated among those states.
 
• The allocation of emoluments and allowances is done in such a proportion as determined by the President of India.
 
• This provision ensures that the financial burden of paying the Governor's emoluments and allowances is shared equitably among the states concerned.
 
• Article 158 also outlines other conditions of the Governor's office, including that the Governor should not be a member of either House of Parliament or a House of the Legislature of any state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: What are the thin filamentous extensions that the motile bacterial cells have from their cell wall called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Flagella**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The thin filamentous extensions that motile bacterial cells have from their cell wall are called **Flagella**.
 
• Flagella are lash-like appendages that protrude from the cell body of certain prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, providing the means for locomotion.
 
• They are essential for the motility of bacteria, allowing them to move toward favorable environments or away from harmful ones.
 
• Flagella are composed of the protein flagellin and are powered by a rotary engine at the base of the flagellum.
 
• They are different from other cell appendages like pili and fimbriae, which are primarily involved in attachment rather than movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pili** are hair-like structures on the surface of bacterial cells that are involved in attachment to surfaces and in the exchange of genetic material during conjugation.
 
• **Fimbriae** are similar to pili but are usually shorter and more numerous, primarily aiding in the attachment to surfaces and to other cells.
 
• **Lamellae** are thin layers, plates, or disks in various biological contexts but are not related to bacterial motility.

questions.question: In which year was ‘Self Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme’ (SHG-BLP) introduced in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1992**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1992** is the year when the 'Self Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme' (SHG-BLP) was introduced in India.
 
• The SHG-BLP is a pioneering initiative by the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) aimed at financial inclusion and poverty alleviation.
 
• This program links self-help groups (SHGs) of rural poor with the formal banking system to provide them with financial services.
 
• It has been instrumental in empowering women and promoting entrepreneurship in rural areas.
 
• The program encourages savings and provides access to credit, enabling SHG members to undertake various income-generating activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The SHG-BLP model has been recognized globally and replicated in several other countries.
 
• As of recent data, millions of SHGs have been linked to banks under this program, benefiting millions of households.
 
• The program has led to significant socio-economic development in rural areas, including improved literacy rates, better health outcomes, and enhanced social cohesion.
 
• NABARD continues to play a crucial role in the expansion and monitoring of the SHG-BLP across India.
 
• The success of SHG-BLP has also led to the introduction of other similar initiatives aimed at financial inclusion and rural development.

questions.question: According to Hindu calendar, Diwali falls in which of the following months?

• The festival signifies the victory of light over darkness, good over evil, and knowledge over ignorance.
 
• It is celebrated with great enthusiasm and involves lighting oil lamps, bursting fireworks, and sharing sweets with friends and family.

• The festival usually falls between mid-October and mid-November, depending on the lunar calendar.
 
• It is also a time for cleaning and decorating homes, buying new clothes, and performing religious rituals.
 
• In addition to Hindus, Diwali is also celebrated by Sikhs, Jains, and some Buddhists.

questions.question: In which Article does the Finance Commission of India find a mention?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 280**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Finance Commission of India is mentioned in **Article 280** of the Constitution of India.
 
• Article 280 mandates the President of India to constitute a Finance Commission every five years or at such earlier time as he considers necessary.
 
• The Finance Commission is responsible for making recommendations on the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Centre and the States, and among the States themselves.
 
• It also advises on measures needed to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of the Panchayats and Municipalities in the state, based on the recommendations made by the State Finance Commissions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body created to address the financial relations between the Centre and the States.
 
• It ensures a fair and equitable distribution of financial resources between the Centre and the States, which is crucial for maintaining fiscal federalism in India.
 
• The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are advisory in nature, but they carry significant weight in the formulation of fiscal policies.
 
• The first Finance Commission was established in 1951 under the chairmanship of K.C. Neogy.
 
• The Finance Commission also reviews the state of finances of the Union and State Governments and suggests measures for maintaining a stable and sustainable fiscal environment.

questions.question: Biological Diversity Act 2002 was passed by the Government of India. It fulfilled ideals of which article of Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 48A**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Biological Diversity Act 2002** was enacted by the Government of India to conserve biological diversity, ensure sustainable use of its components, and ensure fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the use of biological resources.
 
• It fulfills the ideals of **Article 48A** of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution of India.
 
• **Article 48A** states that "The State shall endeavour to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard the forests and wildlife of the country."
 
• The Act provides for the establishment of a National Biodiversity Authority (NBA), State Biodiversity Boards (SBB), and Biodiversity Management Committees (BMC) at local levels.
 
• It aims to regulate access to biological resources and ensure that benefits derived from these resources are shared equitably.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government, and they aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• These principles are not justiciable in a court of law, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The **Constitution of India** was adopted on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950.
 
• It is the longest written constitution of any country in the world and lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishing the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions.
 
• It also sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens, declaring India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four primary explicit goals of five-year plans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Education**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Education** is not one of the four primary explicit goals of the five-year plans in India.
 
• The four primary explicit goals of the five-year plans are **Growth, Equity, Self-reliance, and Modernization**.
 
• These goals aim to ensure balanced economic growth, reduce inequality, achieve self-sufficiency, and modernize various sectors of the economy.
 
• While education is a crucial aspect of development, it is not explicitly listed as one of the primary goals in the context of five-year plans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first Five-Year Plan was launched in **1951** and focused on the agricultural sector.
 
• The concept of Five-Year Plans was inspired by the Soviet model of centralized economic planning.
 
• These plans are formulated, executed, and monitored by the **Planning Commission of India**, which was replaced by the **NITI Aayog** in 2015.
 
• Each plan assesses the country's economic situation and sets targets to achieve desired growth and development.
 
• Over the years, the focus of the five-year plans has shifted according to the changing needs and priorities of the country.

questions.question: As per Article ________ of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers are collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**75(3)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per Article **75(3)** of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
 
• This implies that the entire Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, is accountable to the Lok Sabha for its actions and policies.
 
• If the Lok Sabha passes a vote of no confidence against the Council of Ministers, they must collectively resign.
 
• This collective responsibility ensures that the executive branch of the government is answerable to the legislative branch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of collective responsibility is fundamental to the parliamentary system of government.
 
• It ensures that the executive remains responsible and accountable to the legislature, and through it, to the people.
 
• This principle is essential for maintaining the stability and integrity of the government.
 
• Article 75 of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment, tenure, and responsibilities of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.
 
• Article 75(1) states that the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President, and the other ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
• Article 75(2) mentions that the ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the President.
 
• Article 75(3) establishes the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Select the name of the hydrocarbon with a structural formula CH₃ – CH₂ – CH₂ – CH₂ – CH₂– CH₃.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**n-Hexane**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **n-Hexane** is the name of the hydrocarbon with the structural formula CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃.
 
• It is a straight-chain alkane with six carbon atoms.
 
• The prefix "n-" denotes a normal or unbranched chain structure.
 
• n-Hexane is commonly used in laboratories and industry as a non-polar solvent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hexane** is a significant component of gasoline and is also used as a cleaning agent in the textile, furniture, and leather industries.
 
• It is highly volatile and has a low boiling point, making it useful in various applications but also a potential health hazard if inhaled in large quantities.
 
• Hexane is also used in the extraction of edible oils from seeds and vegetables.
 
• Its chemical formula is C₆H₁₄, and it is part of the alkane series of hydrocarbons.

questions.question: Who among the following envoys was sent by Seleucus I to the court of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Megasthenes** was the envoy sent by Seleucus I to the court of Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• Megasthenes was a Greek historian and diplomat who authored the work **Indica**, which provides valuable information about Mauryan India.
 
• His observations and accounts are considered one of the earliest Western accounts of India.
 
• Megasthenes’ work offers insights into the administration, society, and culture of the Mauryan period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seleucus I Nicator** was one of the generals of Alexander the Great and later founded the Seleucid Empire.
 
• After Alexander's death, Seleucus established control over a vast territory that included parts of the Middle East and Asia.
 
• The alliance and diplomatic relationship between Seleucus and Chandragupta Maurya were significant in shaping the geopolitical landscape of the time.
 
• The **Indica** by Megasthenes, though lost in its original form, survives through quotations by later authors such as Strabo and Arrian.

questions.question: What does M stand for in MUDRA yojana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Micro**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Micro** stands for micro enterprises, which are the primary focus of the MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency) Yojana.
 
• MUDRA Yojana was launched by the Government of India to provide funding to the non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.
 
• The scheme aims to support the growth and development of micro-enterprises in India by providing financial assistance up to Rs. 10 lakh.
 
• MUDRA loans are categorized into three products: Shishu (covering loans up to Rs. 50,000), Kishor (covering loans above Rs. 50,000 and up to Rs. 5 lakh), and Tarun (covering loans above Rs. 5 lakh and up to Rs. 10 lakh).
 
• The initiative is aimed at promoting entrepreneurship and employment generation at the grassroots level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MUDRA Bank** was established as a subsidiary of SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India).
 
• The scheme also focuses on providing financial literacy and credit counseling to micro-entrepreneurs.
 
• MUDRA Yojana is part of the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY), which was launched on 8th April 2015.
 
• It aims to achieve financial inclusion by extending credit to micro-businesses, which often face difficulties in accessing formal banking channels.
 
• The scheme has been instrumental in empowering women entrepreneurs and promoting inclusive growth.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution pertains to the Fundamental Duties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51-A**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51-A** pertains to the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens.
 
• It was added to the Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are intended to serve as a constant reminder to citizens that while enjoying their rights, they also have certain duties to perform towards their country and society.
 
• There are currently **11 Fundamental Duties** listed under Article 51-A.
 
• These duties include respecting the Constitution, cherishing the noble ideals of the freedom struggle, protecting the sovereignty and integrity of India, and promoting harmony.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **42nd Amendment Act**, also known as the "Mini-Constitution," made significant changes to the Indian Constitution, including the addition of Fundamental Duties.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the former Soviet Union.
 
• Although the Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by law, they serve as moral obligations for every citizen.
 
• The idea behind these duties is to encourage responsible behavior and promote a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens.
 
• The **Swaran Singh Committee** was appointed to make recommendations about Fundamental Duties, and many of its suggestions were incorporated into Article 51-A.

questions.question: Which biosphere of Southern Andhra Pradesh is home to many endemic species including the famous Red Sanders and Slender Loris?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Seshachalam** biosphere in Southern Andhra Pradesh is recognized for its rich biodiversity and is home to many endemic species.
 
• This region is particularly famous for the **Red Sanders** (Pterocarpus santalinus), a valuable and rare tree species known for its distinctive red wood.
 
• Another notable species found here is the **Slender Loris** (Loris tardigradus), a small, nocturnal primate that inhabits this unique ecosystem.
 
• The Seshachalam biosphere plays a crucial role in the conservation of these species and their habitats.

• The biosphere reserve covers parts of the **Chittoor** and **Kadapa** districts in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It is part of the Eastern Ghats, which are characterized by their rugged terrain and diverse flora and fauna.
 
• Conservation efforts in this region are aimed at protecting the biodiversity and promoting sustainable development for the local communities.

questions.question: Vasco da Gama, who discovered the sea route from Europe to India, belonged to which nation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Portugal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Vasco da Gama, who discovered the sea route from Europe to India, belonged to **Portugal**.
 
• He was the first European to reach India by sea, linking Europe and Asia via the Cape of Good Hope.
 
• This discovery was significant as it opened the way for an age of global imperialism and for the Portuguese colonial empire to expand in Asia.
 
• Vasco da Gama's journey marked the beginning of a sea-based phase of global multiculturalism and trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Vasco da Gama's first voyage to India was from 1497 to 1499.
 
• He was appointed as the Portuguese viceroy in India in 1524 but died in Cochin (now Kochi) shortly after his arrival.
 
• His successful voyages helped establish a long-lasting colonial empire in Asia for Portugal.
 
• The sea route discovered by Vasco da Gama was instrumental in establishing Portuguese dominance in the Indian Ocean.
 
• His voyages paved the way for the Portuguese to establish a colonial empire in Asia, which included territories in India, Malacca, the Spice Islands, and Macau.

__
 
• **Kathasaritsagara** is a famous literary work originally composed in **Sanskrit**.
 
• It is a renowned collection of Indian legends, fairy tales, and folk tales.
 
• The work is attributed to the author **Somadeva**, who compiled it in the 11th century.
 
• The title "Kathasaritsagara" translates to "Ocean of the Streams of Stories."
 
• This extensive work is an important source for understanding ancient Indian culture and literature.

• It is the liturgical language of Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism.
 
• Many classical Indian texts, including the Vedas, Upanishads, and epics like Mahabharata and Ramayana, were composed in Sanskrit.
 
• Sanskrit literature includes a rich tradition of poetry, drama, scientific, and philosophical texts.
 
• The language has significantly influenced many modern languages in India and around the world.

• He, along with his wife Savitribai Phule, started the first school for girls in Poona (now Pune) in 1848.
 
• Phule's efforts were pioneering in challenging the prevailing caste system and advocating for the rights of the oppressed, including women and lower castes.
 
• His work laid the foundation for subsequent social reform movements in Maharashtra and beyond.

• He was also the founder of the Satyashodhak Samaj (Society of Truth Seekers), which aimed at achieving social equality.
 
• Phule's literary works include the play "Tritiya Ratna" and the book "Gulamgiri" (Slavery).
 
• His contributions to education and social reform have made him a revered figure in Indian history, particularly in Maharashtra.

• Different regions of India celebrate Navratri in different ways, with **Garba** and **Dandiya** being popular in Gujarat and **Durga Puja** being a major celebration in West Bengal.

• **Hirakud Dam:**__

 __
 
• Hirakud Dam is one of the longest dams in the world, with a length of about 25.8 km.
 
• It is a multipurpose dam providing irrigation, flood control, and hydroelectric power.
 
 
 
• **Nagarjuna Sagar Dam:**__
 __
 
• Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is one of the largest and tallest dams in India.
 
• It is primarily used for irrigation and hydroelectric power generation.
 
 
 
• **Sardar Sarovar Dam:**__
 __
 
• Sardar Sarovar Dam is part of the Narmada Valley Project aimed at providing water for drinking, irrigation, and hydroelectric power generation.
 
• The dam has faced significant environmental and social controversies.
 
 
 
• **Tehri Dam:**__
 __
 
• Tehri Dam is the tallest dam in India and one of the tallest in the world.
 
• It is a multipurpose rock and earth-fill embankment dam.
 
 
 
• **Rana Pratap Sagar Dam:**__
 
 
• Rana Pratap Sagar Dam is part of the Chambal Valley Projects.
 
• It provides water for irrigation, hydroelectric power, and industrial use.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of inertia at rest?

options.text: Falling down of dust particle while dusting a cloth
Falling down backward when a vehicle starts immediately
The detachment of leaves/fruits due to shaking
The sudden application of brakes in a vehicle

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Option 4** is NOT an example of inertia at rest. It refers to the sudden application of brakes in a vehicle, which is an example of inertia of motion, not inertia at rest.
 
• **Inertia at rest** is the tendency of an object to remain at rest unless acted upon by an external force.

options.text: a - III, b - IV, c - II, d - I
a - I, b - II, c - III, d - IV
a - II, b - I, c - IV, D - III
a - IV, b - III, c - II, d - I

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A-4, B-3, C-2, D-1.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Faraizi Movement** was founded by **Haji Shariatullah** in the early 19th century. The movement aimed at purifying Islam by eliminating un-Islamic practices among Bengali Muslims. Hence, A matches with 4.
 
• **Mohammedan Literary Society** was established by **Nawab Abdul Latif** in 1863 in Kolkata. The society aimed at promoting modern education among Muslims. Hence, B matches with 3.
 
• **Indian Patriotic Association** was founded by **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan** in 1888. It aimed at creating loyalty among Indians towards the British government and countering the Congress Party. Hence, C matches with 2.
 
• **Wahabi Movement** was led by **Sayyid Ahmad of Rae Bareli** in India. This movement aimed at purging Islam of any un-Islamic practices and restoring it to its original form. Hence, D matches with 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Faraizi Movement:**__

 __
 
• It focused on religious reforms and aimed to remove innovations (bid'ah) and practices considered un-Islamic.
 
• The movement was significant in mobilizing the Bengali Muslim peasantry.
 
 
 
• **Mohammedan Literary Society:**__
 __
 
• It played a crucial role in the social and educational upliftment of Muslims in Bengal.
 
• The society also promoted the use of the English language among Indian Muslims.
 
 
 
• **Indian Patriotic Association:**__
 __
 
• It was an important political organization during the British Raj, advocating for loyalty to the British crown.
 
• The association also worked to counter the influence of the Indian National Congress.
 
 
 
• **Wahabi Movement:**__
 
 
• It was part of the larger Islamic revivalist movement that originated in Arabia.
 
• The movement had a significant impact on the religious and political landscape of India during the 19th century.

questions.question: Which protein is found in grains?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gluten**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gluten** is the main protein found in grains such as wheat, barley, and rye.
 
• It is a composite of storage proteins, namely gliadin and glutenin, which are conjoined with starch in the endosperm of various grass-related grains.
 
• Gluten gives dough its elasticity, helping it rise and keep its shape, and often gives the final product a chewy texture.
 
• While it is a common ingredient in many foods, some individuals have gluten intolerance or celiac disease, which requires them to follow a gluten-free diet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Celiac disease** is an autoimmune disorder where ingestion of gluten leads to damage in the small intestine.
 
• A **gluten-free diet** involves excluding foods that contain gluten, which is found in wheat, barley, rye, and derivatives of these grains.
 
• Gluten-free products are widely available and are essential for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.
 
• Despite its necessity for some, a gluten-free diet is also adopted by others for various health benefits or lifestyle choices.
